articles.title: Pension Is Wall Street's Casino
articles.author: Ellen Brown/Web of Debt
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. “Most billionaires don’t park their money in making more businesses. They park their money in the stock market. That is not meaningfully investing in opportunity, it’s just investing in other billionaires.” So said Abdul El-Sayed , U.S. Senator-elect from Michigan. He said that he would rather “have an economy that makes a thousand millionaires than one billionaire,” and that money that would otherwise go into the S&P 500 should go instead to “good schools, good infrastructure, health care, child care.” It’s a laudable sentiment, but those thousand millionaires would probably still be parking their money in investments designed to make more money without producing anything.

articles.title: Remembering Dolores Huerta (1930-2026)
articles.author: DSA Religion and Socialism Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: Dolores Huerta , who died on October 28 at the age of 96, was an honorary chair of DSA from 2012-2016. But her involvement with our organization went back as far as being a speaker at a 1975 convention of one of DSA’s predecessor organizations. My wife, Dolores Delgado-Campbell, and I met her even earlier,when we were co-chairs of the United Farm Workers (UFW) lettuce boycott committee in Sacramento. We entered the fray in 1972 when the corrupt leadership of the Teamsters Union signed sweetheart contracts with grape growers, committing one of the worst examples of union betrayal in U.S. history. articles.author: Jared Hillel

articles.title: Austerity Is Now the Central Conflict in Brazilian Politics
articles.author: André Singer
articles.content_excerpt: On October 4, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, finished the first round of Brazil’s presidential election nearly two points ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Three weeks later, Lula turned the result around and won a fourth term in the October 25 runoff. In between, left-led demonstrations filled the streets of hundreds of Brazilian cities. The government also banned online betting, backed a forty-hour workweek, and raised the benefit of Bolsa Família, the cash-transfer program for poor families that Lula created in 2003. Few analysts know Lula’s political project better than André Singer. articles.author: Matt McManus
articles.content_excerpt: There is a complex debate about the extent to which socialists prioritize equality above the full flowering of each person’s individuality. articles.title: Working-Class Democratic Candidates Won Big in the Midterms
articles.author: Jared Abbott
articles.content_excerpt: In January, a logger from Maine’s North Woods will take a seat in the US Senate. Troy Jackson spent his adult life cutting timber before he ran for office, and he will be the only Senate Democrat whose working life before politics was spent mostly in a working-class job. But he won’t be alone on Capitol Hill. Across the House, a union ironworker from suburban Cleveland, a Bethlehem firefighter, a Wisconsin waitress, an emergency room nurse, a Montana smoke jumper, a Rochester math teacher, and a former Trader Joe’s worker from Queens are heading to Washington too. By my count, twenty-one Democrats in the next Congress will have spent at least half of their working lives before politics in working-class jobs. Today there are just twelve. articles.title: Steward’s Corner: Rethink the Scripted ‘Ask’
articles.author: Ellen David Friedman
articles.content_excerpt: You’re having a conversation with a co-worker, but inside you’re feeling icy dread. You’re talking through a script that ends with asking them to do a specific thing: sign a union card, wear a button, come to a meeting, vote for a strike. And sure enough, when you ask, a wall comes down. The co-worker looks away, makes an excuse, and pins you as someone who is after something. You’re disappointed, confused about why it didn’t work, and afraid you’re not going to meet your goal. Many of us feel nervous or awkward about asking a co-worker to do something. Sometimes we just need to push ourselves to do it. articles.title: Trump Hurt Average Americans, So They Voted Against the GOP
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: You didn’t even have to look at the numbers on Wednesday to know the election was a rout. You could have just guessed it by the fact that Donald Trump didn’t deny the results, call the whole thing “rigged,” or vow to fight the cheaters to the bitter end. Instead he meekly congratulated the Democrats, insisted none of it was his fault, and offered to work with his opposition before getting back to the truly important work of his ballroom . In a two-week period that saw right-wing leaders across the world refuse to concede and try to find ways to deny election results, Trump, the man who first gave them the playbook to do it, was the only one to accept his defeat. articles.title: The Steel Disaster in Taranto, Italy, Is a Warning to Europe
articles.author: Valentin Vogl
articles.content_excerpt: For decades, labor unions and residents of the southern Italian city of Taranto have been mobilizing around the toxic emissions churned out by the local steel mill. A dedicated group fought for their right to good health through a yearslong legal battle that reached all the way to Italy’s top court. On October 29, the court finally ruled: the blast furnaces, which for decades have blanketed Taranto with fine particulate matter, dioxins, benzene, and asbestos emissions, must close with immediate effect. It represents a bitter-tasting victory after one of the great struggles of European industrial history. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A favorite movie of mine is “ The Cooler ,” starring William H. Macy. Macy plays a sad sack, a loser, a guy down at the mouth and down on his luck. He’s employed as a “cooler” at a casino. Whenever someone is winning too much at the roulette wheel or at craps, Macy goes and stands near the high-rolling winner. Within moments, the high-roller starts to lose, and lose big. Macy is good at his job. Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer are the Democratic Party’s coolers.
